properties.name: Roman Empire at Trajan's accession
properties.note: The provinces of the empire in January AD 98, when Trajan succeeded Nerva. Client kingdoms such as Armenia, Nabataea, Osrhoene and the Bosporan Kingdom are not included.

properties.name: Dacia
properties.note: Conquered from King Decebalus in two hard wars (101–102 and 105–106) and made a province in 106. Hadrian kept it (giving up only the lowlands of Wallachia and southern Moldavia, which are not drawn here); Rome abandoned it c. AD 271–275.

properties.name: Arabia Petraea
properties.note: The Nabataean kingdom was annexed in 106, apparently peacefully, after the death of its last king, Rabbel II; its capital became Bostra. Unlike the eastern conquests, it remained a Roman province for centuries.

properties.name: Armenia
properties.note: Trajan marched in during 114 after Parthia placed its own candidate, Parthamasiris, on the Armenian throne, and made the kingdom a province. Hadrian gave it up in 117–118, returning to a client king.

properties.name: Mesopotamia
properties.note: Overrun in 115–116 as Trajan advanced down the Euphrates and Tigris, took the Parthian capital Ctesiphon and reached the Persian Gulf. Revolts broke out almost at once, and Hadrian abandoned the province in 117–118.

properties.name: Assyria
properties.note: A province named only in late Roman writers; historians disagree whether it lay east of the Tigris (Adiabene, as drawn here) or in Babylonia. Whatever its extent, it was short-lived and Hadrian gave it up in 117–118.

properties.name: Southern Scotland (given up)
properties.note: Part of the province in 98, but the forts of southern Scotland were abandoned c. 105 and the frontier pulled back to the Tyne–Solway line (the Stanegate), later the line of Hadrian's Wall. Not part of the empire at 117.

properties.name: Roman Empire at Trajan's death
properties.note: Convenience outline: empire-98 plus the five acquisitions, minus southern Scotland. Its greatest extent, briefly held.
